The Planner correctly identified the two dates (1216 and 1220) from the WebSurfer results but incorrectly classified the 1216 event as merely an "emergency anointing" and the 1220 event as the "primary coronation." The search results explicitly stated that Henry III was "crowned" on October 28, 1216, at Gloucester Abbey. While the 1220 event was a formal re-coronation, the 1216 event is historically recognized as the actual coronation that established his reign. By dismissing the 1216 date based on the lack of a specific crown or archbishop (which were present in the 1216 event according to the text "with a circlet belonging to his mother"), the Planner contradicted the explicit statement in the source material ("Henry III was crowned on October 28, 1216") and provided an answer (1220) that conflicts with the ground truth provided in the conversation (1216).
